name: security_log_cleared
title: Windows Security Event Log Cleared
why: Log clearing is rarely routine on production hosts and directly destroys audit evidence; any occurrence deserves triage.
fps: Authorised administrators clearing logs during maintenance or log-rotation
Lab/golden-image preparation before telemetry capture (seen in 24 dataset samples)

name: system_log_cleared
title: Windows System Event Log Cleared
why: Same intent as Security log clearing but on the System channel; used to hide service installs and driver loads.
fps: Administrator maintenance
Lab image preparation

name: lsass_suspicious_access
title: Suspicious Process Access to LSASS Memory
why: LSASS holds credential material; broad read/dump rights from non-system binaries are a strong indicator of credential theft.
fps: Endpoint protection / backup agents opening LSASS (add their paths to filter_system)
Crash-dump tooling used by IT

name: regsvr32_scriptlet_exec
title: Regsvr32 Scriptlet Execution (Squiblydoo)
why: Scriptlet loading through regsvr32 bypasses application allow-listing and has few legitimate uses.
fps: Legitimate COM registration with /i: switches by installers (rare, normally no .sct/scrobj)

name: rundll32_proxy_exec
title: Rundll32 Proxy Execution of Script or URL Handlers
why: Several of these exports are legitimate, but combined with rundll32 they are a common LOLBin execution path; medium keeps analyst load manageable.
fps: Software installers calling advpack/setupapi exports
Help/URL handlers invoking url.dll from legacy apps

name: bitsadmin_abuse
title: BITSAdmin Used for Transfer or Persistence
why: BITS is trusted and traffic blends in; /SetNotifyCmdLine specifically gives code execution, so the rule is medium with escalation on notify-cmd.
fps: IT scripts using BITS to distribute software
Legacy deployment tools

name: ifeo_debugger_backdoor
title: Image File Execution Options Debugger Set (Accessibility Backdoor)
why: Debugger hijacks of accessibility binaries give SYSTEM shell at the logon screen; legitimate debugger use is limited to developer machines.
fps: Developers attaching debuggers (WinDbg/Visual Studio) via IFEO on workstations

name: runkey_user_writable_path
title: Registry Run Key Pointing to User-Writable Path
why: User-writable autostart paths are favoured by commodity malware but also used by benign per-user apps, hence medium.
fps: Per-user installers (Teams, OneDrive, Zoom) that auto-start from AppData

name: uac_bypass_registry_hijack
title: UAC Bypass via Registry Shell-Handler Hijack
why: These keys are not modified in normal operation and the technique grants a high-integrity shell without a prompt.
fps: Very rare; some file-association tools modify these keys

name: uac_disabled_enablelua
title: UAC Disabled via EnableLUA Registry Value
why: Disabling UAC removes a core privilege-boundary control and is a deliberate action.
fps: Troubleshooting by administrators; legacy-app compatibility GPOs

name: remote_thread_injection
title: Remote Thread Created in Commonly Injected Process
why: Cross-process thread creation into a victim process is rarely legitimate for these targets.
fps: Accessibility and screen-reader software
Some AV/EDR and game anti-cheat products

name: wmiprvse_suspicious_child
title: WMI Provider Host Spawning Command Interpreter or LOLBin
why: WMI remote execution is a staple of lateral movement but is also used by admin tooling.
fps: Management tools (SCCM, monitoring agents) using WMI to run scripts

name: dcsync_non_machine_account
title: DCSync Replication Rights Used by Non-Machine Account
why: Only domain controllers should replicate; a user account doing so yields all password hashes.
fps: Azure AD Connect / MSOL service accounts that legitimately replicate
Backup or migration tooling with replication rights

name: remote_svcctl_access
title: Remote Service Control Manager Access via SMB (svcctl)
why: Remote service creation is a core lateral movement primitive; admin tooling causes noise so medium until correlated.
fps: Remote administration by IT using sc.exe or management consoles

name: suspicious_service_install
title: Service Installed with Command Interpreter Binary Path
why: Legitimate services point at purpose-built executables, not interpreters.
fps: Admin scripts that register services wrapping cmd (rare)

name: scheduled_task_created_nonms
title: Scheduled Task Created Outside Microsoft Task Path
why: Scheduled tasks are used for persistence and remote execution, but third-party updaters make this noisy; medium.
fps: Software updaters (Chrome, Adobe, Office) creating their own tasks

name: pth_seclogon_logon_type9
title: Pass-the-Hash Style NewCredentials Logon via seclogo
why: Type 9 with seclogo is the signature of credential injection; runas /netonly is the main benign source.
fps: runas /netonly used legitimately by administrators

name: rdp_loopback_tunnel
title: RDP Logon from Loopback Address (Tunnelled RDP)
why: Real RDP clients have a routable source address; loopback implies a tunnel such as SSH/plink/chisel.
fps: Local RDP loopback testing by administrators

name: ps_scriptblock_lsass_dump
title: PowerShell Script Block Dumping LSASS Memory
why: Scripted LSASS dumping has no routine administrative use.
fps: Security tooling / red-team scripts in authorised tests

name: autoelevate_binary_spawns_shell
title: Auto-Elevating Binary Spawning Interpreter (UAC Bypass Child)
why: High-integrity interpreter under an auto-elevating parent is a near-certain UAC bypass.
fps: None expected; these binaries do not normally launch interpreters (eventvwr launches mmc.exe, which is excluded)

name: com_hijack_clsid_user_path
title: COM Object Hijack: CLSID Server Key Pointing to User-Writable Path
why: A CLSID server redirected to a user-writable DLL gives stealthy, logon-triggered persistence; per-user installers are the main benign source.
fps: Per-user installed COM components (e.g., some Office add-ins, Teams/OneDrive shell extensions) register under HKCU with AppData paths

name: lolbin_external_connection
title: LOLBin Initiating Outbound Connection to a Public IP Address
why: These binaries rarely need internet access; connection to a public IP is suspicious but certificate/CRL lookups cause some noise.
fps: certutil used for legitimate CRL/certificate retrieval by some scripts
Software installers invoking rundll32/regsvr32 with network access
